This small plot behind my compound is only a fifth of my land, and I plant it with cassava and cocoyam mixed together like I have always done. The rains here are good, so I do not need to buy fertilizer from the agro-dealer — I put the goat droppings and kitchen ash on the mounds, and that is enough for root crops. I use the cassava cuttings from last year's harvest and the cocoyam suckers my sister gave me, so I do not spend money on seed. My children help me on weekends with the weeding and mounding, and I manage the rest myself.
